### Weighted vs. Unweighted

A weighted graph means there is a value assigned to each edge.
For the solution, you may want to maximize or minimize the total weight of following a path.

For example, selecting your GPS route works as a weighted graph where an edge's weight would indicate the time between the locations (nodes).
Not all routes are equal, and you want the path that requires the shortest time to travel between the destinations you want to visit.
Google Maps would give you the path that minimizes the time (weight) to visit all the locations, which may or may not be the actual shortest path in distance because of other factors such as traffic.
